extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Objects that float and sink — floating means staying on top of water, sinking means going to the bottom. Objects that float: wood, leaf, cork, plastic ball, feather, boat, ice. Objects that sink: stone, coin, iron ball, glass, metal key, gold. (2) Why some objects float and others sink — an object floats if it is LIGHTER (less dense) than water. An object sinks if it is HEAVIER (more dense) than water. Density = how tightly packed the material is. Wood is less dense than water → floats. Stone is more dense than water → sinks. An iron ball sinks (dense and compact), but an iron SHIP floats because it is hollow with air inside and spreads its weight over a large surface area. Air is lighter than water, so hollow objects with air float better. Shape matters: a flat sheet of metal may float but a metal ball sinks. Misconceptions: 'big things always sink' (size doesn't decide — a big log floats, a small coin sinks — it's about density not size), 'heavy things always sink' (a heavy wooden log floats, a light coin sinks — it's about density compared to water, not just weight), 'iron always sinks' (an iron ball sinks but an iron ship floats because of its shape and air inside), 'all plastic floats' (most plastic floats but some dense plastics can sink), 'floating means the object has no weight' (floating objects have weight but the water pushes up with an equal force — this is called buoyancy). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function FloatSinkGame), NOT export default. Export interface FloatSinkGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
